points.description: States that a static array is initialized only once, specifically when the function is called (on first call/entry), not on every call.

levels.says: Says a static array is initialized only once but does not mention the function call or first entry.

points.description: Contrasts with non-static (automatic/local) arrays: they are initialized every time the function is called / each time control enters the block.

levels.says: Says non-static arrays are reinitialized or are not initialized only once, but does not clearly state that this happens on every function call.

points.description: States that a static array retains its values between function calls, whereas a non-static array does not (its values are lost or it is reinitialized on each call).

rubric.notes: Full marks require stating that static arrays are initialized only once (when the function is called) and contrasting them with non-static arrays, which are initialized on every call; also that static arrays retain values between calls. An answer that only describes static arrays without contrasting non-static arrays earns at most the static-array points. No marks for saying static arrays are initialized every time or that non-static arrays are initialized only once.
